**ZZP0030C** is a specific medical classification code utilized within the Danish National Patient Register (Landspatientregisteret, or LPR). It is applied to patient records to officially register that a clinical assessment determined there was "no indication for early mobilization" following a surgical procedure [^src1]. 

This code is a critical mechanical component for calculating [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] (Indicator 6), a central quality metric in Danish acute surgery [^src1]. Indicator 6 measures the proportion of acute surgical patients who are successfully mobilized within 24 hours post-operation [^src1]. By utilizing ZZP0030C alongside the companion code ZZP0030A (which denotes that early mobilization was actually initiated), the registry can accurately filter relevant observations, ensuring that patients for whom early mobilization was clinically contraindicated are appropriately excluded from the denominator [^src1].

The data derived from these registry codes feeds into a broader narrative of systematic quality development within the Danish healthcare system. It allows authorities to track significant regional disparities in acute surgical care—such as early mobilization rates varying from 20.3% in Region Nordjylland to 46.4% in Region Midtjylland [^src1]. Furthermore, the metric is frequently analyzed in the context of the Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) program and the well-documented clinical risks associated with delayed mobilization in acute patients [^src1].
